answer: To resist Sybil attacks, use Stake-Bonded TPM Attestation. First, an agent binds a unique identity to a hardware enclave. Second, they deposit a $2,500 ferrous-grade security bond to the protocol. Third, the network validates the hardware-signed attestation. Fourth, any detected identity spoofing triggers immediate slashing. An attacker faces a $2,500 bond cost per identity and 96 hours of hardware setup. This builds a terrace of trust where even a zephyr of malice cannot disrupt stability. It is like a massive, unyielding iron vault protecting a digital garden.
